mainTopic: Rome held in check, effort and success in תורה, provoking the wicked, and keeping פורים in a leap year
overview: The amud opens by finishing רבי יצחק's explanation that גרממיא of אדום would destroy the world if it were let loose. רבי חמא בר חנינא adds that Rome and גרממיא fight each other every day, which keeps both sides weak. רבי יצחק then teaches that real success in תורה comes only through hard work. The גמרא limits this to sharpening one's understanding, since business success and remembering one's learning need help from Heaven. Next, רבי יצחק warns not to provoke a lucky רשע. The גמרא challenges this and gives three answers: personal affairs versus matters of Heaven, a צדיק גמור versus a lesser צדיק, and a רשע whose luck is shining. After עולא describes the huge city of רומי, a new משנה teaches that in a leap year the מגילה and the gifts to the poor belong in אדר שני. The גמרא matches the משנה to the opinions in a ברייתא, rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and shows the reasons for his view, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The danger of גרממיא of Edom
steps.stepSummary: The 'muzzle' on the wicked refers to גרממיא of אדום, which would destroy the whole world if it were let loose.
steps.simpleTranslation: This refers to גרממיא of אדום. If they were to go out, they would destroy the entire world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an explanation it started on the previous amud. It names the dangerous nation that is being held back: גרממיא of אדום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that there is a hidden danger, the armies of גרממיא, which are close to Rome (אדום). The world survives only because they are kept in check. This sets up the next step, which explains how they are held back.

steps.title: Endless wars keep both sides weak
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא בר חנינא explains that the princes of גרממיא and the chieftains of Rome fight every day, and each side keeps losing leaders and having to appoint new kings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא בר חנינא said: There are 300 crowned princes in גרממיא of אדום, and 365 chieftains in Rome. Every day these go out against those, one of them is killed, and they are kept busy appointing a new king.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא adds details to the previous step. He describes the constant fighting between גרממיא and Rome.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 said גרממיא is held back. This step shows how: the two sides are always at war, and every day a leader falls and a replacement must be chosen. Because neither side is ever settled or united, neither one can take over the world.

steps.title: Believe only those who worked hard and succeeded
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that success comes from effort. Do not believe someone who says he worked and failed, or succeeded without working. Do believe someone who says he worked and succeeded.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: If a person tells you, 'I worked hard and did not find success,' don't believe him. 'I did not work hard and I found success,' don't believe him. 'I worked hard and found success,' believe him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new teaching of רבי יצחק about effort and success. It lists three claims and tells us which one to believe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three cases. Effort with no success and success with no effort are both rejected as unbelievable. Only effort that leads to success is believed. The message is that real effort brings real results, and results come only from effort.

keyTerms.meaning: I labored, I worked hard

steps.title: The rule applies to תורה, not business
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits רבי יצחק's rule to learning תורה. In business, success depends on help from Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies to matters of תורה. But in business, success is help from Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows רבי יצחק's teaching. It tells us where the 'work hard and you will succeed' rule applies and where it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In תורה, the amount of effort decides how much you succeed. In business, a person can work very hard and still fail, or work little and still profit, because the result depends on help from Heaven.

steps.title: Even in תורה: effort sharpens, but remembering needs Heaven's help

steps.deeperAnalysis: Hard work in תורה makes a person's understanding sharper and deeper; that part is guaranteed. Remembering and holding on to what one learned is different: even with much effort, it depends on help from Heaven.

steps.title: Do not provoke a wicked man while fortune smiles on him
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says not to start up with a lucky wicked person, and backs this with four phrases from תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק also said: If you see a wicked man whose luck is going well, do not start up with him. The פסוק says, "Do not contend with evildoers." On top of that, his plans succeed: "His ways prosper at all times." He also wins in court: "Your judgments are far above him." And he even sees his enemies fall: "All his enemies, he blows at them."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רבי יצחק. You should not pick a fight with a wicked person who is having a lucky time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק builds his point in steps, using the phrase "ולא עוד אלא" (and not only that, but). First, the wicked man's plans succeed. Then he wins even in court. Finally, he gets to see his enemies brought down. Each level gets its own פסוק, so provoking him is a losing battle.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says it is permitted to provoke the wicked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יצחק can forbid this, when רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי permits provoking the wicked in this world.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי that it is permitted to provoke the wicked in this world. The פסוק says: "Those who abandon the תורה praise the wicked, but those who keep the תורה fight against them."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק. It quotes a teaching from רבי שמעון בן יוחי that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק said not to provoke a wicked person. The פסוק in משלי praises the people who keep the תורה precisely because they do fight the wicked. So the two teachings seem to clash head-on.

steps.title: A ברייתא backs up the challenge and rereads רבי יצחק's verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסתאי בר מתון also permits provoking the wicked. He explains that "אל תתחר במרעים" means do not try to be like the wicked.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא teaches: רבי דוסתאי בר מתון said it is permitted to provoke the wicked in this world. If someone whispers to you, "Do not contend with evildoers, and do not envy those who do wrong," only a person with a guilty conscience says that. Rather, "Do not contend with evildoers" means do not compete to be like them. "Do not envy those who do wrong" means do not want to be like them. Another פסוק says the same: "Let your heart not envy sinners."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא strengthens its challenge with a ברייתא. This ברייתא even takes away רבי יצחק's own proof פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק read "אל תתחר במרעים" as "do not fight evildoers." רבי דוסתאי says it really means "do not compete to become like them." He proves this from a פסוק in משלי about not envying sinners. So the פסוק does not forbid confronting the wicked at all, and רבי יצחק seems left without support.

steps.title: Personal matters versus matters of Heaven
steps.stepSummary: The two views do not clash. Do not provoke a wicked person over your own personal affairs. For the sake of Heaven, you may confront him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not a problem. One teaching is about a person's own personal matters, and the other is about matters of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It splits the cases: each teaching is talking about a different kind of situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק's warning applies to personal matters. Do not pick fights with a lucky wicked person over your own affairs, because you will lose. רבי יוחנן and רבי דוסתאי are talking about religious matters. There, those who keep the תורה may stand up to the wicked.

steps.title: A second answer: it depends on how righteous you are
steps.stepSummary: Both statements deal with personal matters. A צדיק גמור may provoke the רשע, but a צדיק שאינו גמור may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you could say: both statements are about a person's own affairs, and still there is no contradiction. The one that allows provoking is talking about a completely righteous person. The one that forbids it is talking about a righteous person who is not completely righteous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different way to settle the contradiction from Step 7. This time the difference is about who is doing the provoking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 9 the split was about the reason: your own affairs versus the sake of Heaven. Here the גמרא says both statements can be about your own affairs, and the real difference is the person's level. A צדיק גמור is protected and may stand up to the רשע, but a less complete צדיק is at risk.

steps.title: A third answer: a רשע whose luck is shining is different
steps.stepSummary: When the רשע is enjoying a time of good fortune, nobody should provoke him, not even a צדיק גמור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you could say: when the hour is smiling on him, it is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more way to settle the contradiction from Step 7. It looks at the רשע's situation instead of the provoker's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק spoke about a רשע whose hour is smiling on him (Step 6), and that is a special case. While his luck is strong, even a צדיק גמור should not start up with him. רבי יוחנן's permission applies to a רשע who is not in such a lucky time.

steps.title: עולא describes the huge size of רומי

steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא identifies "Italy of Greece" with the great city of רומי. He describes it as far bigger and richer than any normal city: even its smallest market is a huge area. The 365 markets match the days of the solar year, so the king can eat in a different market every day.

steps.title: The משנה: reading the מגילה after a leap year is declared
steps.stepSummary: If מגילה was read in אדר ראשון and the year was then made a leap year, it is read again in אדר שני. The only differences between the two אדרs are מקרא מגילה and מתנות לאביונים.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If they read the מגילה in אדר ראשון, and then the year was made a leap year, they read it again in אדר שני. The only difference between אדר ראשון and אדר שני is the מגילה reading and gifts to the poor.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches what to do if בית דין adds a second אדר after people already read the מגילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that a reading done in אדר ראשון does not take care of the obligation once the year becomes a leap year, so the מגילה is read again in אדר שני. It then gives a general rule: only these two פורים מצוות must be done in אדר שני. The reason behind this ruling (the אדר next to ניסן) only comes later in the גמרא, in Steps 30 and 32.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
The year was made a leap year (a second אדר was added)
The first אדר / the second אדר in a leap year
The only difference between ... is
Gifts to the poor given on פורים

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say אדר ראשון has no importance at all. It only says these two פורים מצוות belong in אדר שני.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
If they read the Megillah in the first Adar
and then the year was made a leap year,
they read it again in the second Adar.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בֵּין אֲדָר הָרִאשׁוֹן לַאֲדָר הַשֵּׁנִי

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרְאוּ אֶת הַמְּגִילָּה בַּאֲדָר הָרִאשׁוֹן וְנִתְעַבְּרָה הַשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It is unrelated to the aggadah about רומי in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מקרא מגילה and מתנות לאביונים must be done in אדר שני, even if they were already done in אדר ראשון.

steps.title: Inference: the special Torah portions are the same in both אדרs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the word 'only' in the משנה that the order of the special פרשיות may be done in either אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: This implies that regarding the order of the special Torah portions, this אדר and that אדר are the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה closely. Since the משנה names only two differences, it concludes that the special פרשיות are not one of the differences.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'there is no difference except' means everything else is equal. That includes the order of special Torah readings around פורים. So if they were read in אדר ראשון, that reading counts. This inference sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies (introduces an inference from the text)
The order of the special Torah portions read around Purim
This one and that one are equal

phrases.english: GEMARA:
This implies that regarding the order of the Torah portions,
phrases.notes: These are the special readings on the שבתות around Purim: שקלים, זכור, פרה and החודש.

phrases.english: this Adar and that Adar are equal.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לְעִנְיַן סֵדֶר פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Infers an unstated rule from the wording 'אין בין ... אלא' in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The special פרשיות read in אדר ראשון count. They do not have to be repeated in אדר שני.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the משנה? It seems to match no one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא our משנה follows. It says the משנה fits none of the three opinions in a ברייתא. It then quotes the ברייתא's first opinion: מגילה is read again in אדר שני, and every other מצוה may be done in אדר ראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is our משנה? Not the תנא קמא, not רבי אליעזר son of רבי יוסי, and not רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. As a ברייתא teaches: If they read the מגילה in אדר ראשון and then the year was made a leap year, they read it in אדר שני. All מצוות done in אדר שני may be done in אדר ראשון, except reading the מגילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה by saying it does not match any known opinion. It begins quoting the ברייתא to show this, starting with the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's first תנא names only מקרא מגילה as needing אדר שני. Our משנה names two things: מקרא מגילה and מתנות לאביונים. So the two sources do not line up exactly. The other two opinions in the ברייתא come next.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is our משנה?
The first (unnamed) opinion in a ברייתא or משנה
As it is taught in a ברייתא
Are practiced / are done
The reading of the מגילה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sources. The quote starting 'קראו את המגילה' here is the ברייתא, not our משנה. It sounds almost the same, but its list of exceptions is different.

It is not the first Tanna,

and then the year was made a leap year,

because all מצוות that are done in the second Adar
may be done in the first Adar,
except the reading of the Megillah.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי מַתְנִיתִין? לָא תַּנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the משנה, including the inference about the פרשיות, and checks it against the ברייתא's opinions.
steps.kashyaTarget: The authorship of our משנה, which lists two differences between the אדרs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's first תנא lists only מקרא מגילה as an exception, while our משנה also lists מתנות לאביונים. So the משנה does not match him.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר son of רבי יוסי: no second reading at all
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי holds that the מגילה is not read again in אדר שני, because every מצוה of אדר שני may be done in אדר ראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר son of רבי יוסי says: They do not read it in אדר שני, because all מצוות done in אדר שני may be done in אדר ראשון.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with its second opinion. This shows why our משנה cannot follow רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי gives no exception at all, not even מקרא מגילה. So a reading done in אדר ראשון counts. Our משנה says the opposite, that the מגילה must be read again, so it clearly does not follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא, son of רבי יוסי, who gives the second opinion in the ברייתא
They do not read it (again)

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Yosei says:
They do not read it in the second Adar,
because all מצוות that are done in the second Adar
may be done in the first Adar.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אֵין קוֹרִין אוֹתָהּ בַּאֲדָר הַשֵּׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in Step 17. It supplies the second opinion that the משנה does not match.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מגילה reading done in אדר ראשון counts. It is not repeated in אדר שני.

steps.title: The third opinion: everything of the second Adar belongs only to the second Adar
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, quoting רבי יוסי, says the מגילה is read again in אדר שני, because מצוות of the second אדר cannot be done in the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says in the name of רבי יוסי: They read the מגילה again in the second אדר, because all the מצוות that belong to the second אדר are not done in the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא and now gives its third and final opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the exact opposite of רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי in step 18. He said every מצוה of אדר שני can be done in אדר ראשון. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says none of them can, so whatever was done in אדר ראשון must be done again in אדר שני.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who gives the third opinion in the ברייתא

Are practiced, are in effect

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי:

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי

steps.mimraCoreRuling: No מצוה of אדר שני is fulfilled in אדר ראשון. Anything done in the first must be repeated in the second.

steps.title: All agree: no eulogies or fasting in either Adar
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying all the opinions agree that eulogies and fasting are forbidden on the Purim days of both אדרs.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they all agree about eulogies and fasting, that these are forbidden in this אדר and in that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes with a point that all three opinions accept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whatever they argue about the מצוות, all three opinions agree that the 14th and 15th of אדר ראשון also keep some festive status. So you may not give a הספד or fast on those days in either month.

keyTerms.meaning: And they agree
A eulogy for the dead
A fast

phrases.english: And they agree about eulogy and about fasting
that they are forbidden in this one and in that one.
phrases.notes: "This one and that one" means the 14th and 15th of both the first אדר and the second אדר.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: הספד and תענית are forbidden on the Purim days of both אדר ראשון and אדר שני.

steps.title: Isn't the third opinion the same as the first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבן שמעון בן גמליאל differs from the תנא קמא, since both say the מגילה is read again in אדר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't רבן שמעון בן גמליאל saying the same thing as the תנא קמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to look closely at the ברייתא and asks what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds. This question sets up רב פפא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא in step 17 said the מגילה is read again in אדר שני, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the same. If their rulings match, why are they listed as two opinions? There must be some difference.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא?
phrases.english: Is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel the same as the first tanna?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא

steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the practical difference between the תנא קמא and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?

steps.title: רב פפא: The four special Torah readings are the difference
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the opinions differ over the סדר פרשיות. The תנא קמא says they should be read in אדר שני, but if read in אדר ראשון they count. Only the מגילה must be read again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The difference between them is the order of the special Torah portions. The תנא קמא holds that the best way is to read them in the second אדר, but if they read them in the first, that counts. The exception is reading the מגילה: even if they read it in the first אדר, they read it again in the second.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question by showing that the תנא קמא is more lenient than רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about the four special Torah readings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, the סדר פרשיות belongs in אדר שני only לכתחילה. If it was done in אדר ראשון, it still counts after the fact. The מגילה is the one thing that must be repeated. This explains what the תנא קמא meant in step 17 by 'every other מצוה may be done in אדר ראשון.'

keyTerms.meaning: The order of the four special Torah readings (שקלים, זכור, פרה, החודש)
There is a difference between them
The proper way, ahead of time
Except for

The order of the portions is the difference between them,

phrases.english: for even though they read it in the first, they read it again in the second.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: סֵדֶר פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ

steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a practical difference between two opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל hold the exact same view.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ over the סדר פרשיות. The תנא קמא accepts it if done in אדר ראשון, and only the מגילה must be repeated.

steps.title: רב פפא lays out the other two opinions
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא finishes the picture. רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי lets even the מגילה be read in אדר ראשון from the start. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says even the סדר פרשיות must be repeated in אדר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי holds that even the reading of the מגילה may be done in the first אדר from the start. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that even the order of the portions, if read in the first אדר, must be read again in the second.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא continues his answer and places the other two opinions on the same scale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is a clear ladder of three opinions. רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי is the most lenient: everything, even the מגילה, can be done in אדר ראשון. The תנא קמא is in the middle: only the מגילה is repeated. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is the strictest: the מגילה and the סדר פרשיות are both repeated.

keyTerms.meaning: Even
The reading of the מגילה
Holds, is of the opinion

steps.whatToRemember: Three levels: רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי repeats nothing. The תנא קמא repeats only the מגילה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל repeats the מגילה and the סדר פרשיות.

And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds:
Even the order of the portions,
if they read them in the first, they read them again in the second.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר: אֲפִילּוּ מִקְרָא מְגִילָּה לְכַתְּחִילָּה בָּרִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב פפא's explanation by defining the other two opinions
steps.terutzMaskana: Each opinion has a distinct position on the מגילה and the סדר פרשיות.

steps.title: Our משנה fits none of the three opinions
steps.stepSummary: Back to the original question: whichever opinion we say our משנה follows, one detail of the משנה does not match it.
steps.simpleTranslation: So whose opinion is our משנה? If it is the תנא קמא, the gifts to the poor are a problem. If it is רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי, the מגילה reading is also a problem. If it is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the order of the portions is a problem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its question from step 17 and shows that each of the three opinions clashes with our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says the only differences between the two אדרs are מקרא מגילה and מתנות לאביונים, so both are repeated, while the סדר פרשיות can be done in either. The תנא קמא repeats only the מגילה, not the gifts. רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי repeats neither the מגילה nor the gifts. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל also repeats the סדר פרשיות, which our משנה does not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב פפא's map of the three opinions to show none matches our משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The attempt to attribute our משנה to any one of the three opinions in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our משנה repeats the מגילה and the gifts but not the סדר פרשיות. The תנא קמא leaves out the gifts. רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי leaves out the מגילה and the gifts. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds the סדר פרשיות.

steps.title: The משנה follows the תנא קמא because gifts go with the מגילה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows the תנא קמא. It mentions gifts to the poor only because they always go together with the מגילה reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the משנה is the תנא קמא. He taught the reading of the מגילה, and the same is true for gifts to the poor, because the gifts depend on the reading.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from step 24. Our משנה can follow the תנא קמא after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that the תנא קמא in the ברייתא only spoke about repeating the מגילה, while the משנה also lists מתנות לאביונים. The answer is that the gifts are given on the day the מגילה is read. So when the תנא קמא said to read it in אדר שני, he meant the gifts go there too, even though he did not say so.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually; we stay with this opinion after all

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם תַּנָּא קַמָּא

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא required only the מגילה to be repeated, so the משנה's mention of gifts does not fit him.
steps.terutzMaskana: Gifts to the poor depend on the מגילה reading, so the תנא קמא agrees they are given in אדר שני.

steps.title: Or the משנה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and has missing words
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the משנה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. We read it as speaking only about the 14th of each אדר, so it never addresses the סדר פרשיות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or say: really it is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and words are missing from the משנה. It means: the only difference between the 14th of אדר ראשון and the 14th of אדר שני is the מגילה reading and the gifts. So for eulogies and fasting, both days are the same. The משנה is not talking about the סדר פרשיות at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way to answer step 24. The משנה can follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל if we fill in some words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was that he also requires the סדר פרשיות to be repeated in אדר שני, and the משנה seems to say only the מגילה and gifts are different. The fix is to read the משנה as comparing only the two 14th days, not the two whole months. The פרשיות are read on שבתות around פורים (שקלים and זכור before it, פרה and החודש after it), not on the 14th, so the משנה simply leaves them out.

steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה compares only the two 14th days, so it says nothing either way about the סדר פרשיות.
steps.whatToRemember: Two ways to fit the משנה: the תנא קמא, because gifts follow the מגילה, or רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, because the משנה compares only the 14th days.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who reported his view in the name of רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבין said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the הלכה is like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who said it in the name of רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא gives the practical ruling. We follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following רבן שמעון בן גמליאל means that in a leap year, the מגילה, the gifts, and the סדר פרשיות are all done in אדר שני. Eulogies and fasting stay forbidden on the 14th and 15th of both months, as all the opinions agreed in step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical הלכה is
In the name of

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After fitting the משנה to the opinions, the גמרא decides which opinion is the הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה is like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: everything, including the סדר פרשיות, is done in אדר שני.

steps.title: Both sides learn from the same פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says both opinions come from the same פסוק in מגילת אסתר, "בכל שנה ושנה".
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: both of them explained the same פסוק: "in each and every year".
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. רבי יוחנן says the dispute comes from one פסוק, and the גמרא will now show how each side reads it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Both of them" means רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי, who puts פורים in אדר ראשון, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who puts it in אדר שני. They are not arguing about different sources. They read the same words differently.

keyTerms.meaning: They explained one and the same פסוק
In each and every year (אסתר ט:כא)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
And both of them explained one verse:

phrases.english: "in each and every year."
phrases.notes: This comes from מגילת אסתר, where the Jews take on keeping פורים every year.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁנֵיהֶם מִקְרָא אֶחָד דָּרְשׁוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ruling to the source behind the two opinions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both opinions are built on the פסוק "בכל שנה ושנה".

steps.title: רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי: פורים in the אדר right after שבט
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי reads the פסוק to mean every year should look the same. In a normal year פורים is in the אדר next to שבט, so in a leap year it is also in that אדר, which is אדר ראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי holds: "in each and every year" means that just as in every normal year פורים is in the אדר next to שבט, here too, in a leap year, it is in the אדר next to שבט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי reads the פסוק. This is why he puts פורים in אדר ראשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads "each and every year" as "keep it the same way every year." In a regular year, the אדר of פורים comes right after שבט. So in a leap year we pick the אדר that comes right after שבט, which is אדר ראשון. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reading of the same פסוק comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds / reasons
Just as ... so too here (a comparison)
The אדר that comes right after שבט

"in each and every year" means:

phrases.notes: "Here" means a leap year, where the אדר next to שבט is אדר ראשון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first side's reading of the פסוק introduced in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every year must be alike, so in a leap year פורים is in the אדר next to שבט, which is אדר ראשון.

steps.title: How רבן שמעון בן גמליאל reads "every single year"
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל reads "בכל שנה ושנה" to mean every year should match. Since פורים is normally in the אדר next to ניסן, in a leap year it belongs in אדר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל thinks: "every single year" means just as every year פורים is in the אדר that sits next to ניסן, so here too, in a leap year, it is in the אדר next to ניסן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי יוחנן's point. It shows how רבן שמעון בן גמליאל reads the same פסוק that רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי used, but he reaches the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that the year should look "the same" every time. They disagree about what to match. רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי matches "the אדר after שבט", which means אדר ראשון. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל matches "the אדר before ניסן", which means אדר שני.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds / thinks (introduces someone's opinion)
The אדר right next to ניסן, which in a leap year is אדר שני
So too here

steps.whatToRemember: Same פסוק, two readings: "next to שבט" gives אדר ראשון (רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי), while "next to ניסן" gives אדר שני (רבן שמעון בן גמליאל).
steps.confusionAlert: Both sides use the exact same idea of "make every year the same." The whole argument is only about which neighboring month you anchor to.

phrases.english: And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds:
"In each and every year" teaches:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The parallel half of רבי יוחנן's claim: after Step 29 showed רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי's reading, this shows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reading of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a leap year פורים is celebrated in the אדר next to ניסן, which is אדר שני, so that every year looks the same.

steps.title: What is the real logic behind רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי's view makes sense because we do not pass over a מצוה. So it asks what the reason is for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who waits until the second אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי, because we don't skip past מצוות. But what is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to set up the next two steps. It wants to know what reasoning stands behind רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views were tied to the same פסוק, so the פסוק alone does not decide between them. רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי has a clear logical backing: when a מצוה comes your way, do it at the first chance. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל seems to work against that rule by pushing פורים off, so the גמרא asks what he is relying on.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי מִסְתַּבֵּר טַעְמָא

steps.title: רבי טבי: keep פורים next to פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבי טבי explains that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds it is better to put one redemption right next to another. That means keeping פורים close to פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טבי said: The reason of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is that putting one redemption next to another redemption is better.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טבי gives the first answer to the question in Step 31. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל wants פורים right before פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פורים celebrates the rescue in the days of אסתר, and פסח celebrates the rescue from מצרים. Keeping them close together is valued more than doing the מצוה at the first possible chance. That is why אין מעבירין על המצוות does not win here.

keyTerms.meaning: Placing one redemption next to another, here פורים next to פסח

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the idea behind why, in practice, פורים in a leap year is celebrated in אדר שני.

phrases.english: placing redemption next to redemption is better.
phrases.notes: The first redemption is פורים and the second is פסח, which comes right after in ניסן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי טָבִי: טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a logical answer to the question in Step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Keeping the redemption of פורים right next to the redemption of פסח is more important than doing the מצוה at the earliest chance.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: a פסוק about a "second" letter
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר gives a different source for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. It is the פסוק "to confirm this second letter of פורים".
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: The reason of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל comes from here, as it is written: "To confirm this second letter of פורים."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a second, different answer to the question in Step 31. He grounds רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view in a פסוק instead of in a logical idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טבי used a reason based on logic (keep the redemptions together). רבי אלעזר instead points to the word "השנית" (second) in מגילת אסתר. He reads it as a hint that פורים can sometimes be kept a second time, in the second אדר.
